summary: Iteration 3 replaces the placeholder field-library with the full Canonical Writing Model (13 domains loaded as DATA) and splits domain-independent reasoning from domain-specific knowledge. Rewrote the backend pytest suite for the new schema (telos / theory / theory_history / interactions replacing the old dev_state fields) and ran 7 test cases. 6/7 pass. Backend logic itself is correct — verified by hitting the internal server on localhost:8001 where a full two-turn flow (writing + revise) completes in 49s + 79s and produces (a) currently_relevant_domains drawn from the 13 canonical names, (b) 2-3 candidate_invitations and one selected_invitation per turn, (c) a growing theory_history that snapshots the PREVIOUS theory before each update (v1 then v2), (d) changes_since_previous transitioning off 'initial' after the second turn, (e) no stage/level/score/rubric language anywhere, (f) revise turns acknowledged rather than denied, and (g) teacher can revise the telos via PATCH with a teacher_edits audit record + GET returning the revised values. Frontend end-to-end verified via Playwright on the public URL: TeacherSetup → Begin Session → StudentWorkspace with no route change, first draft receives one ai-invitation bubble, dev panel exposes 'Currently Relevant Canonical Domains', 3 candidate-invitation-N cards, 'Selected Invitation', 'Change From Previous Interaction'; telos editor toggles, saves, and a 'Telos revised' toast fires; reload persistence works (localStorage dws_session_id restores the conversation). ONE CRITICAL FINDING: the second /api/sessions/{id}/interact call consistently returns 502 through the Cloudflare-fronted public URL (dev-converse.preview.emergentagent.com) even though the internal backend answers in ~80s. Reproduced 3× (each with 2 automatic retries). Root cause is that _build_prompt now embeds the entire canonical_writing_model.json (~13 large domain records) into the prompt on every turn, so the LLM turnaround for later turns exceeds Cloudflare's ~60s edge idle-timeout on this preview. This is a real UX regression for multi-turn sessions in production and needs an app-layer fix (see action items). The one failing backend pytest — TestSecondInteract::test_second_interact_revises_theory_and_history — fails ONLY because of that 502, not because of an engine defect.

critical.issue: Second (and subsequent) interact calls return 502 Bad Gateway from Cloudflare when routed through the public URL. Internal backend at localhost:8001 answers correctly (~79s) but the edge timeout kills the request. Root cause: _build_prompt embeds the FULL canonical_writing_model.json (13 domains, ~5-8KB of JSON) plus growing theory + history + interactions on every turn, so per-turn LLM latency climbs past ~60s. Reproduced 3× consecutively via direct requests to the public URL (second interact: 502 in 60.2s, 195.4s, 60.6s). Fix candidates: (a) don't re-send the full canonical JSON every turn — send only relevant domain names + a short signature and rely on Claude's prompt caching / SYSTEM_MESSAGE for the rest; (b) pre-filter to the currently_relevant_domains from the last theory before injecting into the next prompt; (c) stream the LLM response so the connection stays warm; (d) if the edge timeout is fixed, raise it above 90s.

minor.issue: Still returns 200 instead of 201 for resource creation (carried over from iteration_1 / iteration_2, non-blocking).

No server-side retry / backoff around chat.send_message — a single flaky LLM call surfaces as HTTP 502 to the client. Wrapping run_engine() in a small (1-2 attempt) retry on transient exceptions would soften this.

integration_issues.issue: Because the backend's second interact 502s on the public URL, students hitting a second turn on production will see the 'The coach could not respond' toast (App.js line ~52). First turn UX is fine; second-turn failure is systematic, not flaky. Same root cause as the backend critical item above.

issues: Repeat of iteration_1 / iteration_2 finding: the sliding dev panel (max-w-md, fixed right-0) overlays the sticky right-hand 'Conversation with your coach' column instead of being an offset drawer or pushing content. Content is still readable but the right ~30% of the workspace is hidden by the panel — see /app/.screenshots/dev_panel_open.png. Not blocking, but visible.

action_items: CRITICAL: shrink the per-turn LLM prompt so multi-turn interactions do not hit the ~60s Cloudflare edge timeout on the public URL. The safest change is to NOT resend the entire canonical_writing_model.json each turn — instead, either (a) inject only the domain names + a one-line description into every user prompt and keep the full model in SYSTEM_MESSAGE where prompt caching applies, or (b) pre-filter down to `session.theory.currently_relevant_domains` (plus 1-2 candidate neighbours) before injecting. Aim for a per-turn total prompt < 6KB and per-turn LLM wall-clock < 45s.
Add a light retry (1-2 attempts, 3-5s backoff) around chat.send_message in run_engine so an occasional upstream hiccup doesn't propagate as an HTTP 502.

Optional carry-overs (unchanged from prior iterations): return 201 from POST /api/sessions; either push the workspace left or use a smaller panel width so the dev panel doesn't overlay the sticky conversation column at ~1920px; add a length cap on writing-area / reply-input to bound prompt size.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:_build_prompt (line ~278-295): the full CANONICAL_WRITING_MODEL dict is dumped into the user prompt with json.dumps(..., indent=2) on EVERY turn. That is the direct cause of the 502 regression under Cloudflare. The canonical model is also static and cacheable — belongs in SYSTEM_MESSAGE (with prompt caching) or in a compact form (domain_name + one-line function summary + `possible_developmental_invitations` first entry) rather than the full JSON blob per turn.

server.py: SYSTEM_MESSAGE and the theory schema look correct for the 'domain-independent engine + domain-specific canonical model' split. currently_relevant_domains, candidate_invitations (2-3), selected_invitation (coherence not optimality), observed_reorganization, and changes_since_previous are all wired through the recursive-loop instructions and the Pydantic models. Verified by internal-backend two-turn run: domains chosen were legitimate canonical names ('Whole Essay Purpose', 'Central Claim / Thesis', 'Paragraph Purpose', 'Interpretation / Reasoning'), 3 candidate invitations were generated, theory_history preserved v1 (empty defaults) then v2 (first-turn theory).

server.py:interact (line ~426-432): theory_history snapshot is correctly taken with the CURRENT session.telos/theory BEFORE the update is applied — this preserves the previous theory rather than overwriting it. Snapshot version numbering (len(theory_history)+1) is correct.

server.py:edit_telos: teacher_edits records the diff (from/to) per changed field, the telos mirror is updated consistently, and telos.telos_changed is set to a non-empty marker. GET after PATCH returns the revised values — verified by pytest TestTelosEdit.
server.py:run_engine: no retry, no timeout ceiling, and no length cap on `req.content`. A very long submission plus the full canonical JSON could push prompt tokens past reasonable limits.

DevelopmentPanel.jsx: TelosEditor only exposes assignment / pedagogical_purpose / current_writing_task — it does NOT expose teacher_notes, so the teacher can't edit them from the panel even though the backend accepts them. Minor gap.
StudentWorkspace.jsx (line 246): the helper text now reads 'Revise here with the revise mode, or edit your draft on the left and send it again.' — accurate; iteration_2 nit resolved.

App.js: no visible retry on failed interact; the user just gets 'The coach could not respond. Please try again.' with no way to auto-recover the pending turn. Combined with the 502 issue above this is a poor experience on second-turn.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_developmental_engine.py (rewritten for the new schema — telos / theory / theory_history / interactions replacing dev_state / primary_developmental_tension / etc.; added assertions for canonical domain membership, 2-3 candidate invitations, observed_reorganization, theory_history preservation, no stage/score language, teacher-edit telos flow, 404 on missing session for GET / PATCH / POST interact, and a retry wrapper for transient 502s from the public URL)

success_rate.backend: 86% (6/7) — the 1 failure is the Cloudflare 502 on second interact via public URL, NOT an engine defect; direct localhost:8001 run passes all logic
success_rate.frontend: 100% of critical single-turn flows and dev-panel + telos-editor + reload-persistence flows

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the pytest suite serially (pytest -n 0) — module-scoped fixtures + pytest.<attr> pass state between classes. Full run is ~4 min because Claude turns are 45-80s each with the current large prompt. The ONE flaky failure (TestSecondInteract) is a real production issue, not a test-bug: second interact via the public URL returns Cloudflare 502 because per-turn LLM latency exceeds the edge timeout. Direct localhost:8001 works. Once E1 shrinks the per-turn prompt (see action_items[0]), re-run and expect 7/7. If you want to bypass the flakiness while E1 works on the fix, run against http://localhost:8001 directly.
rca of the issue: Regression cause: iteration_3 loads canonical_writing_model.json (13 richly-structured domain records) and _build_prompt embeds the ENTIRE model as pretty-printed JSON into the user prompt on every /interact call. Combined with the growing theory + participation history + reorganization history, the per-turn prompt is ~5-8KB just from the canonical model alone, and grows across turns. Claude Sonnet 4.6 latency for this prompt is ~45-80s per turn (measured directly against localhost:8001: 49.1s for turn 1 and 79.2s for turn 2). The public URL sits behind Cloudflare with an approximately 60s edge idle-timeout, so second-turn responses arrive AFTER Cloudflare has already returned a 502 to the client. Direct backend calls succeed and produce fully-correct output (verified: currently_relevant_domains populated with canonical names, 2-3 candidate invitations, theory_history v1 preserves the empty initial theory, changes_since_previous is not 'initial' after the revise turn, no stage/score language). Mitigation for E1: (a) move the canonical model into SYSTEM_MESSAGE (so Anthropic prompt caching applies, cutting subsequent-turn latency substantially), OR (b) pre-filter the canonical model to `session.theory.currently_relevant_domains` plus 1-2 close neighbours before embedding, OR (c) send only a compact index (domain_name + first canonical resource) and let the engine ask for detail via a follow-up field. Also add a small retry+backoff around chat.send_message so transient 5xx from the LLM provider don't propagate. Once per-turn wall-clock stays comfortably under ~45s, the second-interact 502 disappears and TestSecondInteract will go green.
